children: The collaboration will focus on multidisciplinary treatment, advanced diagnostics, precision oncology and coordinated patient-care pathways across South Mumbai

HCG Cancer Hospital, Colaba and Asian Cancer Institute (ACI) – Cumballa Hill Hospital have entered into a strategic collaboration in Mumbai to expand access to comprehensive cancer care by integrating their clinical expertise, infrastructure, technology and specialist capabilities. Announced on 16 September, 2026, the partnership will focus on coordinated diagnosis, treatment planning and multidisciplinary cancer management.

The collaboration will cover surgical, medical and radiation oncology, advanced diagnostics and pathology, precision and personalised treatment approaches, and access to advanced cancer technologies. The hospitals also plan to strengthen patient navigation, supportive and palliative care, rehabilitation and survivorship services.

The institutions said the partnership will use multidisciplinary tumour board-based decision-making to bring specialists together for treatment planning. It will also include initiatives around clinical quality, patient safety, outcomes, academic programmes, training and knowledge sharing.

“At HCG, we have always believed in ‘adding life to years’ as one of our key philosophies when approaching cancer treatment,” said Dr. B.S. Ajaikumar, Non-Executive Chairman, HealthCare Global Enterprises Limited. He added that the partnership aims to reduce fragmentation between different stages of cancer treatment and improve coordination among specialists.

Dr. Ramakant Deshpande, Executive Chairman, Asian Cancer Institute, said the collaboration would bring together complementary capabilities to create a more integrated cancer-care platform in Mumbai. “Cancer treatment today requires more than individual clinical interventions. It demands multidisciplinary expertise, advanced technology, evidence-based protocols and seamless coordination across specialties,” said Dr. Manish Mattoo, Executive Director and CEO, HealthCare Global Enterprises Limited.

The partnership is expected to establish standardised clinical pathways and continuous quality-improvement processes across participating services. According to the institutions, the model will cover the cancer-care continuum from early diagnosis and multidisciplinary evaluation through surgery, medical and radiation oncology, diagnostics, supportive care, rehabilitation and survivorship.

“The partnership is designed to create a seamless continuum of cancer care spanning early diagnosis, multidisciplinary evaluation, surgical oncology, medical oncology, radiation oncology, advanced diagnostics, supportive care, rehabilitation and survivorship,” said Rupesh Choubey, Vice President – Regional COO, Maharashtra & MP, HCG Cancer Hospital. The two institutions also plan to explore expansion of specialised oncology services, strengthen specialist networks and introduce additional treatment capabilities for patients in Mumbai and the surrounding region.
